newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta dockyard orders pick up.
newsitem.headline: Malta dockyard orders pick up.

text.p: The loss-making Malta Drydocks has reported a full order book for the next two months, with contracts with British, U.S., Tunisian, Chilean and Algerian companies and good prospects for orders from Iran.

The company's general manager, Spiro Aquilina, said most of the year so far had been generally good for the yard, particularly in view of its successful tendering for repairs to P&O's flagship liner Royal Viking Sun after it ran aground close to the Suez Canal. Work on the liner was completed in record time in June and won accolades for the yard.

Aquilina said the yard's docks were full. A major job on P&O's large container ship Moretin Bay is about to be completed, and another P&O container ship, Botany Bay, is due in the first week of September. The yard is also expected to win a third contract for works on Discovery Bay.

The dockyard has works in hand on World Process, owned by the Greek Niarchos line, White Sea of OMI line of New York, the Algerian-owned Balabbes the Tunisian-owned Nebhana and Sea Ford of Greek-owned Marinter Shipping. The Chilean-owned vessel Loa is due on Wednesday.

Aquilina did not give details on the value of the contracts but said the dockyard was planning to build on its worldwide reputation and he would shortly be heading a delegation to Teheran to negotiate more contracts with that country. A dockyard delegation would also visit Japan, Hong Kong, Singapore and India.
"We cannot expect work orders to come on their own" Aquilina said.

State-owned Malta Drydocks, which amalgamated with the tiny state-owned Malta Shipbuilding yard last year, employs 3,500 workers and is run in a unique worker-participation system where the members of a council elected by the workers are effectively the directors of the company.
The government is giving the yard Lm13 million ($36.4 million) in direct subsidies this year.
